recent_posts.title: I'm Making Headway Now
recent_posts.summary: A post on reddit claimed that my module JSON::Parse was not only failing some of the JSON Test Suite tests, but also crashing on one of them. I found that after 80,000 open brackets the stack was overflowing, causing the crash to occur. If I added a printf in the midst of my code the printf would cause the stack overflow, so it wasn't actually due to my code.

recent_posts.title: Perl weekly challenge 093
recent_posts.summary: This is a Raku answer for the 093 Perl Weekly Challenge. This is also my first post. The solution looks at points with equal slope to see if they are in a straight line. The binary tree has been defined as 'lines of nodes', with 0 if the node is empty. The representation of the tree is: 1 2 3 4 0 5 6.

top_posts.title: First Perl Steering Council elected to replace Pumpking position

top_posts.title: Why you should use ppport.h in your XS code modules
top_posts.summary: ppport.h is a file that is part of the Devel::PPPort distribution. It implements portions of the API that people have found desirable to have when a module gets installed in a Perl that was released before that API element was created. You can write your moduleusing the latest API, and have it automatically work on old Perls, simply by including ppport.h in your code.

top_posts.title: Opt-in your CPAN repos for Hacktoberfest
top_posts.summary: Hacktoberfest has become opt-in, to reduce spammy pull requests. If you've got repos with issues that you'd be happy to receive pull requests on, add the topic hack toberfest and make sure your repo turns up in searches. You can find Perl repos that have been opted in using these two terms in their search box:language:Perl topic:hacktoberFest.
